title: The City That Tried to Cool One Street
passage:
A shopping street in Midori City became uncomfortably hot each summer. The road was narrow, buildings stood close together, and very little shade reached the pavement in the afternoon. Shop owners complained that customers avoided walking there during the hottest hours. The city could not easily widen the street or plant large trees because underground pipes and building entrances left little space.

Officials first considered coating the pavement with a light-colored material designed to reflect more sunlight. Laboratory tests suggested that the surface itself could stay cooler. Several residents supported the idea, but an urban climate researcher warned that surface temperature and human comfort are not identical. A brighter road may reflect heat away from the pavement yet send more radiation toward people and nearby walls. Wind, humidity, and shade also affect how hot a person feels.

The city decided to run a small experiment on one hundred meters of the street. Half received the reflective coating, while the other half remained unchanged. Sensors measured surface temperature, air temperature, wall temperature, and humidity. Volunteers also walked both sections at different times and recorded how hot they felt.

The coating worked in one sense: on clear afternoons, the treated pavement was often ten degrees cooler than the untreated section. Air temperature a meter above the road, however, changed very little. People walking in direct sun did not always report feeling cooler. Some even said the brighter surface felt harsh on the eyes. The experiment showed that lowering one temperature number did not automatically improve the whole experience.

The city added a second measure. Shop owners were offered small grants for retractable awnings that could extend over part of the sidewalk without blocking emergency access. Because the street was narrow, the awnings could not cover everything, but they created short shaded sections in front of stores. Benches were moved into those shaded areas, and drinking-water stations were placed near the busiest points.

The following summer, volunteers repeated the comfort survey. The combination of cooler pavement and shade produced better results than the coating alone. Yet the effect varied by time of day. In the morning, when buildings already cast shadows, the awnings mattered little. In the late afternoon, they made a clear difference. On very humid days, even shaded areas felt uncomfortable.

The project changed the way officials described the goal. At first they had spoken of ‘reducing street temperature,’ as if one number represented the problem. Later they spoke of ‘reducing heat exposure for pedestrians.’ That broader goal allowed several smaller interventions to work together.

The city did not cover every street with reflective material. It used the treatment only where measurements showed strong afternoon heating and where glare would not create problems. Awnings were encouraged on streets with heavy pedestrian use. The lesson was not that reflective pavement worked or failed. It worked for a specific physical effect, but that effect was only one part of human comfort. The project succeeded when the city stopped searching for a single cooling technology and began treating heat as a system involving surfaces, shade, air, movement, and people.
translation:
緑市のある商店街は夏になると非常に暑く、午後には日陰がほとんどなくなるため、店主たちは客足が落ちると訴えていました。道路は狭く、地下配管や建物入口もあるため、大きな木を植えるのは難しい場所でした。

市はまず、太陽光を反射しやすい明るい舗装材を使う案を考えました。実験室では路面温度を下げる効果がありましたが、都市気候の研究者は『路面温度が下がることと、人が涼しく感じることは同じではない』と指摘しました。反射した熱が人や壁へ向かう可能性があり、風、湿度、日陰も体感に影響するからです。

そこで百メートルだけ試験し、半分を反射舗装、半分を従来舗装にしました。路面、空気、壁、湿度を測り、歩行者にも体感を記録してもらいました。晴れた午後、反射舗装の路面は十度ほど低いこともありましたが、地上付近の空気温度はほとんど変わらず、直射日光下では必ずしも涼しく感じられませんでした。明るすぎてまぶしいという意見もありました。

市は次に、店先へ出せる収納式の日よけに補助金を出しました。道路全体は覆えませんが、短い日陰を連続して作り、ベンチや給水場所もそこへ移しました。

翌夏の調査では、反射舗装だけよりも日陰との組み合わせの方が快適さを改善しました。ただし効果は時間帯で異なり、建物の日陰がある朝は小さく、午後遅くには大きくなりました。湿度が非常に高い日は、日陰でも不快さが残りました。

市は目標の言い方も変えました。最初は『道路温度を下げる』でしたが、後には『歩行者が受ける暑さを減らす』となりました。この広い目標に変えることで、複数の対策を組み合わせられました。

最終的に反射舗装を全市へ広げることはせず、午後の加熱が強く、まぶしさの問題が少ない場所に限定しました。重要なのは、反射舗装が成功か失敗かという二択ではありません。特定の物理的効果には成功しましたが、人の快適さはそれだけでは決まりません。表面、日陰、空気、人の移動を一つの仕組みとして考えたとき、初めて実用的な暑さ対策になったのです。

title: Why the Hospital Changed Its Appointment Reminder
passage:
A regional hospital had a persistent problem with missed appointments. Patients sometimes forgot their scheduled time, arrived on the wrong day, or failed to cancel when they could not come. Empty appointment slots were difficult to fill at the last minute, while other patients waited weeks for care. The hospital already sent reminder text messages twenty-four hours before each visit, but the missed-appointment rate remained higher than staff wanted.

Administrators initially proposed sending more reminders: one week before, three days before, one day before, and again on the morning of the appointment. A behavioral researcher working with the hospital questioned whether more messages would help. If patients began seeing reminders as routine background noise, extra messages might reduce attention rather than increase it.

The hospital reviewed a sample of missed appointments. Forgetting was only one cause. Some patients had transportation problems. Some were unsure whether they would be charged for canceling. Others tried to call the hospital during busy periods, could not get through, and then gave up. A reminder that simply repeated the date and time did not address these obstacles.

A new message was designed. It still gave the appointment details, but it also included a clear cancellation link and a short statement: ‘If you cannot attend, canceling today helps another patient use this time. There is no cancellation charge.’ Patients who had registered a preference for phone contact received an automated call with the same information.

The hospital tested the new message in several departments. Cancellation rates increased at first, which worried some staff because it looked like more patients were dropping appointments. However, many cancellations happened two or three days in advance, giving staff time to offer the slot to someone on a waiting list. The number of appointments that were simply missed without notice fell.

The hospital then tried adding a transport-help link for patients in departments where travel difficulties were common. This produced a smaller but meaningful improvement. Not every problem could be solved by messaging. Some patients still faced sudden illness, work emergencies, or family responsibilities. The goal shifted from eliminating missed appointments to reducing avoidable ones.

After six months, the hospital sent fewer total reminder messages than the original ‘more reminders’ proposal would have required, yet it recovered more usable appointment time. Staff also spent less time making follow-up calls.

The project taught administrators that communication should not be judged by how often a message is sent. A reminder works only if it addresses the decision the recipient needs to make. The original message assumed the main problem was memory. The new system recognized that patients might remember perfectly and still face uncertainty about cancellation, transport, or procedure. By studying why appointments were missed, the hospital changed the content rather than simply increasing the volume. More communication was not the answer; more relevant communication was.
translation:
地域病院では予約の無断欠席が続き、空いた枠を直前に埋められない一方、別の患者は何週間も待っていました。病院はすでに前日にSMSを送っていましたが、欠席率は十分下がりませんでした。

そこで一週間前、三日前、前日、当日朝と何度も送る案が出ました。しかし行動研究者は、通知が増えすぎると背景の雑音になり、かえって注意されなくなる可能性を指摘しました。

無断欠席の例を調べると、原因は忘却だけではありませんでした。交通手段の問題、キャンセル料金がかかると思っている人、電話が混んでつながらず諦めた人などがいました。日時を繰り返すだけの通知では、こうした障害は解決できません。

新しい通知には日時に加え、簡単なキャンセルリンクと『来られない場合、今日キャンセルすると別の患者がこの時間を使えます。キャンセル料はかかりません』という説明を入れました。電話連絡を希望する患者には同じ内容の自動音声を使いました。

試験すると、最初はキャンセル件数が増え、職員の一部は悪化したように感じました。しかし多くは二、三日前に行われ、その枠を待機患者へ回せました。一方、何の連絡もなく来ないケースは減りました。

交通問題が多い診療科では支援情報へのリンクも追加しました。効果は小さめでしたが改善がありました。ただ、突然の病気、仕事、家族事情などメッセージでは解決できない欠席もあります。そのため目標は『欠席ゼロ』ではなく『避けられる欠席を減らす』へ変わりました。

六か月後、当初案より少ない通知数で、実際に使える予約時間を多く回収でき、職員の確認電話も減りました。

この経験から、連絡は回数だけで評価できないと分かります。通知は相手が必要な判断に役立って初めて意味があります。以前は『忘れている』ことを主原因と考えていましたが、覚えていても、キャンセル方法や費用、交通に不安があれば行動できません。なぜ欠席するのかを調べたことで、量ではなく内容を変えることができました。必要だったのは『より多い連絡』ではなく『より関係のある連絡』だったのです。

title: The River Project That Used Three Kinds of Evidence
passage:
Residents of a town downstream from a forest complained that the river had become muddier after heavy rain. Some blamed recent logging on nearby hills. The forestry company argued that all cutting followed regulations and that storms had simply become more intense. Both sides had photographs supporting their views, but the pictures had been taken on different days and at different places. The town council wanted evidence strong enough to guide action rather than deepen the argument.

A university team proposed using three kinds of information. First, automatic sensors would measure water cloudiness at fixed points every hour. Second, rainfall records would show how much rain had fallen before each change in the river. Third, field teams would inspect several slopes and streams for exposed soil, drainage problems, and erosion. No single source would be treated as sufficient.

The first months produced confusing results. Cloudiness increased after large storms even in areas without recent logging. This supported the company's claim that rainfall mattered. Yet two smaller storms caused unusually muddy water in one branch stream below a newly built forestry road. Field inspection found that a drainage ditch beside the road was sending concentrated runoff toward an unstable slope.

The forestry company repaired the ditch and added barriers to slow the water. During later storms of similar size, cloudiness in that branch stream was lower. The improvement suggested that the road had contributed to at least part of the problem. However, the university team warned against concluding that all river mud had one cause. Other tributaries still became cloudy after intense rainfall because of natural soil movement and older erosion sites.

The town council used the results to change its policy. Instead of debating whether forestry as a whole was ‘the cause,’ it required stronger drainage checks for new roads and additional monitoring after construction. It also began restoring vegetation along two older eroded banks unrelated to current logging.

Some activists felt the council had been too cautious because they wanted stricter limits on tree cutting. Some industry representatives felt the monitoring focused unfairly on forestry. The researchers responded that their task was not to distribute blame equally or choose a political compromise. It was to identify what the evidence could and could not support.

After two years, the river still became muddy during major storms, but several local spikes were reduced. More importantly, the debate changed. Residents, officials, and the company now looked at the same time-stamped data rather than comparing isolated photographs. Disagreement did not disappear, but it became more specific.

The project showed why environmental questions often require multiple kinds of evidence. A sensor can show when water changes but not necessarily why. Rainfall records can reveal patterns but not locate a damaged slope. Field inspection can identify a plausible source but may miss what happens during a storm. When the three sources were combined, the town could move from a broad argument about a whole industry toward targeted actions supported by evidence.
translation:
森林の下流にある町で、大雨後の川が以前より濁るという苦情が出ました。住民の一部は最近の伐採を原因と考え、林業会社は規則を守っており、豪雨が強くなったことが主因だと主張しました。双方に写真はありましたが、撮影日や場所が違い、比較できませんでした。

大学チームは三種類の証拠を組み合わせました。固定地点の濁度センサー、降雨量記録、そして斜面や支流を直接調べる現地調査です。どれか一つだけで結論を出さない方針でした。

最初の数か月では、最近伐採していない地域でも大雨後に濁度が上がり、雨量の影響が大きいことが確認されました。一方、ある新設林道の下流支流では、それほど強くない雨でも異常な濁りが二回発生しました。現地調査すると、道路脇の排水溝が水を一か所へ集め、不安定な斜面へ流していました。

会社が排水路を修理し、水を弱める設備を入れると、同程度の雨でもその支流の濁りは低下しました。林道が問題の一部だった可能性は高まりましたが、研究者は『川全体の濁りがすべて林道原因』とは結論しませんでした。他の支流では、強い雨による自然な土砂移動や古い侵食箇所も影響していたからです。

町は『林業全体が原因かどうか』という議論から離れ、新設林道の排水確認を厳しくし、工事後の監視を増やしました。同時に、現在の伐採とは無関係な古い河岸侵食の修復も始めました。

活動家の一部は伐採規制が弱いと感じ、業界側は林業ばかり調べられると不満を持ちました。研究者は、役割は責任を均等配分することではなく、証拠が何を示し、何を示せないかを明確にすることだと説明しました。

二年後も大雨では川は濁りますが、局地的な急上昇のいくつかは減りました。さらに、議論は単独写真ではなく同じ時刻付きデータを基に行われるようになりました。

この事例は、環境問題に複数の証拠が必要な理由を示します。センサーは変化の時刻を示しても原因までは分からず、雨量記録は傾向を示しても壊れた斜面の場所は特定できません。現地調査も嵐の最中の変化を見逃すことがあります。三つを組み合わせたことで、広い責任論から、証拠に基づく具体的な対策へ進めたのです。

title: The Company That Stopped Rewarding Only Speed
passage:
A customer-support company measured how quickly employees completed each call. The metric was easy to collect, and managers believed shorter calls meant higher efficiency. Teams with the lowest average call time received monthly recognition. Over time, employees learned to finish conversations quickly, sometimes before customers fully understood the solution.

Complaints began rising. Customers called back about the same problem, and some cases were transferred repeatedly between departments. Managers initially responded by giving employees new scripts designed to make explanations shorter. Average call time improved again, but repeat calls continued.

A data analyst compared individual call time with what happened afterward. She found that very long calls were sometimes inefficient, but extremely short calls had a higher chance of producing another contact within forty-eight hours. A five-minute call followed by two more five-minute calls was not more efficient than one ten-minute conversation that solved the problem. The original metric counted only the visible first interaction.

The company created a broader measure called ‘resolved contact.’ A case counted positively when the customer did not need to return about the same issue within two days. Call time remained visible, but it was no longer the main target. Managers also reviewed customer satisfaction and transfer rates.

The change had unintended effects. Some employees began keeping customers on the line longer than necessary because they feared a repeat contact. The company clarified that long calls were not automatically better. Supervisors listened to samples and looked for whether the employee understood the issue, explained the next step clearly, and checked that the customer knew what to do. Training focused on judgment rather than hitting one number.

Within several months, average call time increased slightly. If managers had looked only at the old metric, performance would have appeared worse. Yet total call volume decreased because repeat contacts fell. Customer complaints also declined. Staffing costs did not drop immediately because the company used the freed capacity to reduce waiting time during busy periods.

The experience changed how managers thought about measurement. A metric can become harmful when people begin optimizing the number instead of the real goal. Call time had originally been a rough sign of efficiency, but once rewards were attached to it, employees naturally learned to make the number look good. That behavior was rational within the system even when it produced poor service.

The company did not stop measuring speed. Long calls can still signal confusing processes or inadequate tools. Instead, speed became one clue among several. The central question changed from ‘How quickly did we end this call?’ to ‘Did we solve the customer's problem with reasonable use of time?’ That wording was less simple and harder to measure, but it better represented what the company actually wanted. The case showed that easy-to-measure numbers are useful only when managers remember they are indicators of a goal, not the goal itself.
translation:
あるカスタマーサポート会社では、通話を何分で終えたかを効率の指標にしていました。測定が簡単で、平均通話時間が短いチームを毎月表彰していたため、社員は会話を素早く終えるようになりました。しかし、顧客が十分理解する前に通話を終えるケースも増えました。

同じ問題で再度電話する顧客や、部署間を何度も転送されるケースが増えました。会社は最初、説明を短くする新しい台本を作りましたが、通話時間は改善しても再連絡は減りませんでした。

データ担当者が調べると、極端に短い通話ほど四十八時間以内の再連絡率が高い傾向がありました。五分の通話を三回するなら、一回十分で解決する方が全体として効率的です。従来の指標は最初の通話しか見ていませんでした。

そこで『解決済み連絡』という考えを導入し、二日以内に同じ問題で再連絡がなければ高く評価するようにしました。通話時間も残しましたが、中心指標ではなくし、満足度や転送率も確認しました。

すると今度は、再連絡を恐れて必要以上に通話を長くする社員も現れました。会社は『長いほどよい』わけではないと説明し、問題理解、次の手順の明確さ、顧客が理解したかの確認などを通話サンプルで評価しました。単一数字ではなく判断を訓練する方向へ変えました。

数か月後、平均通話時間は少し長くなりました。旧指標だけなら悪化に見えます。しかし再連絡が減って総通話件数が下がり、苦情も減りました。空いた能力は混雑時間の待ち時間短縮に使われました。

この経験から、測定値に報酬を強く結び付けると、人は本来の目的ではなく数字そのものを最適化し始めることがあると分かりました。通話時間は効率の手掛かりではありますが、目標そのものではありません。会社は速度測定をやめず、複数の手掛かりの一つとして扱いました。問いも『何分で切ったか』から『適切な時間で顧客の問題を解決したか』へ変わりました。測りにくくても、実際の目的に近い問いの方が重要だったのです。

title: The Forest Path That Was Closed to Recover
passage:
A popular forest trail led to a waterfall and attracted thousands of hikers each year. Over time, the soil on several steep sections became deeply worn. Rainwater followed the depressed path, washing away more soil and exposing tree roots. Park managers repaired the trail repeatedly, but each busy season damaged the same places again.

The simplest response seemed to be stronger construction. Some proposed stone steps and wooden barriers along the entire route. Ecologists warned that extensive construction could disturb the forest and move water problems elsewhere. They suggested closing one damaged section for a full year and redirecting hikers along a longer route.

Local businesses opposed the idea. The alternative trail added twenty minutes to the walk, and café owners feared visitors would choose another destination. Hikers also complained online that public land should remain accessible. Managers held meetings and explained that the proposed closure covered only eight hundred meters, not the entire forest.

Before deciding, the park tested smaller controls. Signs asked hikers to stay on the center of the trail, and ropes blocked informal shortcuts. Volunteers repaired drainage channels. These measures slowed damage but did not reverse it. During wet weekends, hundreds of boots still pressed soft soil into the same narrow area.

The park eventually approved a nine-month closure beginning after autumn leaves ended. Workers did not rebuild the whole section. They redirected runoff with small channels, added fallen branches to discourage walking, and planted local ground vegetation where soil remained. The goal was to let natural recovery do part of the work. Cameras counted wildlife and checked whether people entered the closed area.

Recovery was uneven. Some exposed soil developed plant cover within months, while the steepest slope remained fragile. Heavy rain damaged one newly planted area, requiring another season of protection. The closure was extended for three months. This frustrated businesses because they had planned around the announced reopening date. Park staff admitted that ecological recovery did not follow a calendar exactly and began giving ranges rather than fixed promises.

When the section reopened, the trail was slightly rerouted around the most vulnerable slope. Visitor numbers returned quickly. Businesses reported a short-term loss during closure but not a permanent decline. The park also introduced a seasonal rule: during several weeks of very wet spring weather, the fragile section could close temporarily.

The experience forced the community to confront a difficult idea. Access can damage the very place people want to access. Keeping a trail open every day may seem to serve visitors, but if erosion eventually makes the route unsafe, everyone loses access for longer. Closing it temporarily was not the opposite of public use; it was one way of preserving future use. The challenge was deciding how much present inconvenience was justified by uncertain long-term benefit. There was no perfect answer, but monitoring recovery allowed the park to adjust rather than rely on either unrestricted access or permanent closure.
translation:
人気の森林遊歩道は滝へ続き、毎年多くの登山者が訪れていました。しかし急斜面の土が深く削れ、雨水がそのくぼみを流れてさらに土を流し、木の根まで露出するようになりました。毎年修理しても、繁忙期になると同じ場所が傷みました。

石段や木製設備で強化する案が出ましたが、生態学者は大規模工事が森林を乱し、水問題を別の場所へ移す可能性を指摘しました。代わりに一部区間を一年ほど閉鎖し、長い迂回路へ誘導する案を提案しました。

地域の店は反対しました。迂回で二十分長くなれば観光客が他へ行くかもしれません。登山者からも公共の森を閉じることへの不満が出ました。管理者は閉鎖範囲が全体ではなく八百メートルだと説明しました。

まず小さな対策として、中央を歩く案内、近道を防ぐロープ、排水路修理を行いました。しかし湿った週末には何百人もの靴が同じ土を踏み、劣化を止めきれませんでした。

最終的に紅葉期後から九か月閉鎖しました。全区間を人工物で作り直すのではなく、小さな排水路を作り、倒木で立ち入りを防ぎ、在来植物を植えて自然回復も利用しました。

回復速度は場所によって違いました。数か月で植物が戻る場所もあれば、急斜面は弱いままで、大雨で植栽が流れた場所もありました。そのため閉鎖を三か月延長しました。店側には不満が出ましたが、管理者は生態系が予定表どおり回復するわけではないと認め、以後は再開時期を幅で示すようにしました。

再開時には最も弱い斜面を避けて少し経路を変更し、春の非常に湿った数週間は一時閉鎖できる制度も導入しました。客数は戻り、地域の店への影響も永久的ではありませんでした。

この経験は、『利用することが、利用したい場所を傷つける』という難しい問題を示しました。毎日開け続ければ利用者に親切に見えますが、侵食が進めば将来もっと長く閉じることになります。一時閉鎖は公共利用の反対ではなく、未来の利用を守る方法でもあります。現在の不便と不確実な将来利益をどう比べるかに完全な答えはありませんが、回復を測りながら調整することで、全面開放か永久閉鎖かの二択を避けることができました。

title: The Teacher Who Changed How Homework Was Counted
passage:
A mathematics teacher gave students ten short homework problems each night. Completion was recorded, and students received points for submitting all ten. The system seemed fair because everyone received the same work and the same scoring rule. Yet the teacher noticed a pattern: some students copied answers when they were tired rather than leave problems blank and lose completion points.

The teacher first considered checking work more strictly. That would increase the risk of copying being caught, but it would also require much more grading time. More importantly, she wondered whether the scoring system itself encouraged students to hide what they did not understand. A blank answer communicated difficulty, while a copied answer looked complete. The incentive favored appearance over information.

For one month, she tested a different system. Students still received ten problems, but they could mark up to two with a question symbol instead of giving an answer. To receive full completion credit, they had to write one sentence explaining where they became stuck. During the next lesson, the teacher chose several common question-mark problems for review.

Some students initially used the option simply to avoid difficult work. Their explanations were vague, such as ‘I don't get it.’ The teacher clarified that a useful note had to identify a step: ‘I can expand the brackets, but I don't know how to combine these terms,’ for example. She did not require long writing; she wanted evidence of where understanding stopped.

The quality of homework changed. There were more visible incomplete problems, which at first made the class results look worse. However, copied-looking answer patterns decreased, and students asked more specific questions. The teacher also discovered topics that had seemed well understood under the old completion system but were actually confusing many students.

Not every student liked the change. High-performing students said the question-mark system was unnecessary for them. A few students still copied work. The teacher kept the option voluntary and continued occasional checks. Her purpose was not to create a perfect anti-cheating system. It was to make honest uncertainty less costly.

At the end of the term, test scores were slightly higher, but the teacher did not claim the homework policy alone caused the improvement. Many factors affected learning. She valued another result more: class discussions became easier because students were willing to show partial understanding.

The experiment changed what ‘complete homework’ meant. Under the old rule, completeness meant every box contained an answer. Under the new rule, a page could be complete even if two answers were missing, provided the student had genuinely attempted the work and identified the difficulty. The teacher learned that assessment systems do more than measure behavior. They shape which behavior students believe is safe to reveal. If a system punishes visible confusion more than hidden copying, it may accidentally make learning harder to observe.
translation:
数学の先生は毎晩十問の短い宿題を出し、十問すべて提出すると提出点を与えていました。全員同じ課題と基準なので公平に見えましたが、疲れた生徒が空欄で減点されるのを避けるため、答えを写しているような例が見られました。

先生は監視を厳しくすることも考えました。しかし採点負担が増えるだけでなく、そもそも制度が『分からないことを隠す』方向へ生徒を押しているのではないかと考えました。空欄は困難を正直に示しますが、写した答えは完成して見えます。

そこで一か月、十問のうち最大二問まで答えの代わりに？印を付けても満点の提出点を認める仕組みを試しました。ただし、どの段階で止まったか一文で説明する必要があります。翌日の授業では、共通して多かった？問題を取り上げました。

最初は『分からない』だけで済ませる生徒もいました。先生は『展開はできるが、その後どう整理するか分からない』など、理解が止まった場所を示すよう求めました。長文を書く必要はなく、思考の境目が見えればよいのです。

宿題には目に見える未完成が増え、一見すると成績が悪化したように見えました。しかし不自然に同じ答えを書く例は減り、質問は具体的になりました。以前は理解できているように見えた単元で、多くの生徒が実は困っていたことも分かりました。

成績上位者には不要だという意見もあり、一部の写しは残りました。制度は任意のままにし、確認も続けました。目的は完全な不正防止ではなく、正直な『分からない』のコストを下げることでした。

学期末のテストは少し上がりましたが、先生は制度だけの成果とは主張しませんでした。それより、部分的な理解を生徒が見せやすくなり、授業で扱いやすくなったことを重視しました。

この実験で『宿題を完成する』意味が変わりました。以前はすべての欄に答えがあることでしたが、今は本当に取り組み、どこで止まったか示せば、答えが二つなくても学習として完成と考えます。評価制度は行動を測るだけでなく、何を見せても安全かという感覚も作ります。混乱を見せることの方が写すことより強く罰される制度は、学習の実態を見えにくくしてしまうのです。

title: The Bridge That Needed Fewer Warning Signs
passage:
A pedestrian bridge over a railway line had a low beam near one entrance. Tall cyclists who rode across the bridge sometimes hit the beam if they did not lower their heads. Riding bicycles on the narrow bridge was already prohibited, and several warning signs told cyclists to get off and walk. Despite the signs, some continued riding. The city responded after each minor accident by adding another warning.

Within a few years, the entrance contained six different signs: ‘Walk Your Bicycle,’ ‘Low Clearance,’ ‘Slow Down,’ ‘Watch Your Head,’ a height measurement, and a picture of a bicycle with a red line through it. Officials assumed more warnings meant more safety. Residents complained that the entrance looked confusing and that none of the signs stood out.

A safety engineer reviewed the site. She agreed that cyclist behavior was part of the problem but questioned the sign strategy. People approaching the bridge had only a few seconds to notice, read, and act. Six competing messages required more attention than one clear instruction. She also noticed that the bridge entrance visually resembled the continuation of the bicycle path. Nothing in the physical design strongly suggested that riders should stop.

The city tested a redesign. Most signs were removed. A single large ground marking said ‘DISMOUNT’ with a bicycle symbol before the entrance. A short textured strip made the surface feel different under wheels, and a narrow railing created a slight turn that encouraged cyclists to slow down. One height warning remained beside the low beam.

Some residents worried that removing signs would reduce legal protection or make the danger less visible. The city checked the required safety standards and kept the mandatory notices, but eliminated duplicated messages that were not required. Accident reports and video observations were collected for six months.

The number of cyclists entering at full speed decreased. Not everyone dismounted, but more slowed before reaching the beam. Near-miss incidents also fell. Researchers could not say which part of the redesign produced most of the change because the signs, pavement, and railing were altered together. The city accepted this limitation because the practical goal was safer behavior, not proving the effect of one element.

The project challenged the assumption that adding information always increases safety. A warning competes for limited attention. When many warnings overlap, each may become less noticeable. Physical design can also communicate expected behavior before words are read. The new entrance made slowing down feel natural rather than relying entirely on obedience to signs.

The engineer emphasized that fewer signs should not become a universal rule. Some hazards genuinely require several kinds of information. The lesson was more careful: every warning should have a clear purpose, and repeated warnings should not substitute for fixing confusing design. Safety communication is strongest when the environment, the instruction, and the action people need to take all point in the same direction.
translation:
線路をまたぐ歩道橋の入口近くには低い梁があり、自転車に乗ったまま通る背の高い人が頭をぶつけることがありました。橋は狭く自転車走行は禁止されており、『降りて押してください』などの看板もありましたが、事故のたびに市はさらに警告看板を追加していました。

数年後、入口には『自転車を押す』『頭上注意』『減速』『低い梁』『高さ表示』『自転車禁止マーク』など六種類が並びました。情報を増やせば安全になると考えられていましたが、住民からは多すぎて何も目立たないという声が出ました。

安全技術者が見ると、接近する数秒の間に六つの内容を読み行動するのは難しく、さらに自転車道がそのまま橋へ続いて見えるため、物理的にも『ここで止まる』という印象が弱いことが分かりました。

そこで大部分の重複看板を外し、入口手前の路面に大きく『降りる』と自転車マークを表示しました。車輪で分かる質感の違う帯を置き、短い柵でわずかに進路を曲げ、自然に減速するようにしました。低い梁の高さ警告は残しました。

看板を減らすと法的に問題ではないかという心配もありましたが、必要な表示は残し、義務でない重複だけを外しました。六か月の観察では高速のまま入る自転車が減り、降りない人でも減速する割合が増え、接触寸前の例も減りました。複数要素を同時に変えたため、どれが最も効いたかは断定できませんが、実際の安全改善が目的なので市はその限界を受け入れました。

この事例は、情報を増やせば安全が高まるとは限らないことを示します。警告は限られた注意力を奪い合い、多すぎると一つ一つが弱くなります。また、言葉を読む前に物理的環境そのものが行動を伝えることもできます。

ただし『看板は少ないほどよい』という一般則ではありません。複数情報が必要な危険もあります。大切なのは、各警告に明確な役割があり、重複看板で分かりにくい設計を隠さないことです。環境、指示、必要行動が同じ方向を示すとき、安全な伝達は最も強くなります。

title: The Student Survey That Changed Its Own Question
passage:
A group of students wanted to know whether classmates were satisfied with school lunch. They created an online survey with a simple question: ‘Do you like school lunch?’ Respondents could choose yes or no. More than seventy percent selected yes, and the group planned to report that the lunch program was highly successful.

Their social studies teacher asked them to look at the written comments before finishing. The comments did not fit neatly with the number. Some students who answered yes complained that portions were too small. Others liked the food but disliked the short eating time. A few who answered no actually enjoyed most meals but had allergies that limited their choices.

The students realized that ‘school lunch’ contained several different experiences: taste, nutrition, portion size, variety, eating environment, and access for dietary needs. Their yes-or-no question had forced all of those into one response. The seventy-percent figure was not false, but it was too broad to guide improvement.

They designed a second survey. This time students rated several aspects separately on a five-point scale and could choose ‘not applicable’ when necessary. The survey also asked one open question: ‘What single change would improve lunch most for you?’ Before sending it schoolwide, the group tested it with twelve students. Two questions used words that younger students interpreted differently, so the wording was revised.

The new results were more complicated. Taste received generally high ratings, but variety was lower. Eating time was a major concern among students whose classrooms were farther from the cafeteria. Portion satisfaction differed by age and activity level. Students with dietary restrictions gave high ratings to staff helpfulness but lower ratings to choice.

At first, the group missed the simplicity of their original result. A single percentage was easy to put on a poster. The new data required explanation and did not produce a clear ‘good’ or ‘bad’ verdict. Yet it led to more useful recommendations. The school could not change every issue immediately, but it adjusted the lunch schedule for two distant classrooms and began testing an optional extra serving of rice on certain days.

The students also learned to be cautious about comparisons. Because the second survey asked different questions, they could not claim that satisfaction had increased or decreased from the first survey. The two instruments measured different things. They kept the first result in their report but explained its limitation.

The project taught them that survey quality depends on the question before it depends on the number of responses. A thousand answers to a vague question can still produce vague knowledge. Measurement begins by deciding what exactly is being measured. Their first question had been convenient because it produced a clear statistic. Their second survey was harder to summarize, but it respected the complexity of the experience they wanted to understand. Sometimes better evidence makes a story less simple rather than more certain.
translation:
生徒グループが『学校給食に満足しているか』を調べるため、『給食は好きですか』というはい・いいえのオンライン調査を行いました。七割以上が『はい』だったため、給食制度は非常に成功していると報告しようとしました。

しかし先生に自由記述を見るよう言われると、数字と合わない内容が多くありました。『好き』と答えた人でも量が少ない、食べる時間が短いと不満があり、『嫌い』と答えた人の中には、味は好きでもアレルギーで選択肢が少ない人がいました。

生徒たちは、『給食』には味、栄養、量、種類、食事環境、食事制限への対応など複数の要素があると気づきました。最初の質問はそれらを一つの答えに押し込んでいました。七割という数字は間違いではありませんが、改善には使いにくい情報でした。

二回目は各項目を五段階評価にし、必要なら『該当しない』も選べるようにしました。また『一つだけ変えられるなら何を変えたいか』という自由記述も入れました。全校配布前に十二人で試すと、年齢によって解釈が違う言葉があり、表現を直しました。

新しい結果は複雑でした。味は高評価、種類はやや低く、食堂から遠い教室では食事時間への不満が強く、量の満足度は年齢や運動量で違いました。食事制限のある生徒は職員対応を高く評価する一方、選択肢には不満がありました。

最初の一つの数字の方がポスターには簡単でしたが、新しい調査の方が具体的対策につながりました。遠い教室の昼休み開始時刻を調整し、一部の日にご飯のおかわりを試すことになりました。

また、二つの調査は質問が違うため『満足度が上がった・下がった』とは比較できないことも学びました。最初の結果も報告書に残しましたが、限界を説明しました。

この活動から、調査の質は回答数より前に『何を質問するか』で決まると学びました。曖昧な問いに千人が答えても、得られる知識は曖昧です。良い証拠は必ずしも物語を単純にするとは限らず、むしろ現実の複雑さを正しく見せる場合があります。

title: The Coastal Town That Raised One Road
passage:
A coastal town experienced repeated flooding during strong storms. Seawater and rainwater collected on a low road connecting the harbor to the main highway. When the road closed, fish deliveries were delayed and residents in one neighborhood had to take a long detour. Engineers proposed raising the road by nearly one meter.

The plan seemed straightforward until residents from streets behind the road objected. They feared the higher road would act like a wall, trapping rainwater on the inland side. Engineers replied that new drainage pipes would carry water under the road, but residents pointed out that existing drains often became blocked by leaves and sand during storms. A design that worked only when every drain remained clear might fail at the worst moment.

The town created a detailed flood model and combined it with records from past storms. Raising the road reduced seawater crossing from the harbor, but the model confirmed that inland water could rise if drainage capacity was insufficient. Engineers added larger culverts and a small pumping station, increasing the project's cost.

Some council members questioned whether the town should spend so much on one road when climate projections suggested future storms could become even stronger. They proposed moving harbor facilities instead. Business owners argued that relocation would be far more expensive and could weaken the local fishing economy. The debate became less about engineering and more about how long the town expected existing infrastructure to remain important.

The final project raised only the most vulnerable section of road rather than the entire route. Drainage channels were redesigned so they could be inspected easily, and sensors reported water levels during storms. The town also created a maintenance schedule that increased drain cleaning before the typhoon season. Emergency plans still included road closure because officials did not claim the new design could prevent every flood.

Two years later, a strong storm tested the system. Seawater did not cross the raised section, and the road remained open longer than it had in similar past storms. Inland water rose but stayed below house entrances. The pumps operated for several hours. Officials called the result encouraging but not proof that the town was now safe. One storm could not represent every future condition.

The project demonstrated why adaptation to climate risk rarely has a permanent finish line. Infrastructure can reduce risk without eliminating it. Raising the road changed where water could move, which created new responsibilities for drainage and maintenance. The town had to judge cost, present economic needs, and uncertain future conditions at the same time.

Residents eventually accepted that the question was not ‘Can we stop flooding?’ but ‘Which failures can we reduce, and what risks remain after we do so?’ That question was less comforting, but it led to more honest planning. The road project became one layer of protection among monitoring, maintenance, emergency closure, and longer-term discussion about the harbor's future.
translation:
海沿いの町では強い嵐のたびに、港と幹線道路を結ぶ低い道路が海水と雨水で冠水していました。閉鎖されると魚の配送が遅れ、住民も大きく迂回する必要がありました。技術者は道路を約一メートル高くする案を出しました。

しかし道路の内陸側に住む人々は、高い道路が壁になって雨水を住宅側へ閉じ込めるのではないかと心配しました。技術者は道路下の排水管を増やすと説明しましたが、住民は既存排水口が葉や砂で詰まることを指摘しました。すべての排水口が常に正常であることを前提にする設計は、最悪の嵐で弱い可能性があります。

洪水モデルと過去記録を組み合わせると、道路を上げれば港側からの海水流入は減る一方、排水能力が不足すると内陸の水位が上がることが確認されました。そのため大きな暗渠と小型ポンプ場を追加し、費用は増えました。

議会では、将来さらに強い嵐が予想される中、一つの道路へ大金を使うべきかという議論も起きました。港施設そのものの移転案も出ましたが、事業者は費用と地域漁業への影響を懸念しました。議論は工学だけでなく、現在の港を何年使い続けるのかという地域の将来像にも関わりました。

最終案では全線ではなく最も低い区間だけを上げ、点検しやすい排水路、水位センサー、台風前の清掃強化を組み合わせました。すべての洪水を防げるとは言わず、緊急閉鎖計画も残しました。

二年後の強い嵐では、上げた区間を海水が越えず、道路は過去の同程度の嵐より長く利用できました。内陸側の水位は上がりましたが住宅入口までは達せず、ポンプも数時間作動しました。町は良い結果と評価しながらも、一回の嵐で将来の安全を証明できるとはしませんでした。

この事例は、気候への適応に『完成』がないことを示します。道路を高くするとリスクは減りますが、水の流れが変わり、排水と維持管理という新しい責任が生まれます。町は『洪水を完全に止められるか』ではなく、『どの失敗を減らせるか、その後どのリスクが残るか』を考えるようになりました。道路は監視、清掃、緊急閉鎖、港の将来検討と並ぶ、複数の防御策の一層になったのです。

title: The Reading Program That Counted the Wrong Success
passage:
A city library created a summer reading program for children. Participants received one stamp for every book they finished, and prizes were given after ten, twenty, and thirty books. Registration grew quickly. At the end of summer, officials proudly reported that children had read more than twelve thousand books, twice the number from the previous year.

Several librarians, however, noticed behavior that made them question what the total meant. Some children selected only very short books near the end of the program to reach the next prize. Parents occasionally returned large stacks and asked for stamps even when children could say little about the books. None of this clearly broke the rules. The program had defined success as completed book count, so families naturally responded to that target.

The library did not want to test children after every book. Turning voluntary summer reading into an exam might reduce enjoyment. It also did not want to discourage short books, which can be valuable and appropriate for many readers. The problem was not that certain books counted too easily. The problem was that one number had become the entire meaning of participation.

The next summer, the library redesigned the program around reading experiences rather than total books. Children still collected stamps, but stamps came from different activities: finishing a book, trying a new genre, reading with another person, visiting a nonfiction shelf, or sharing one sentence about a favorite part. There was a maximum number of stamps available from simple book completion, so reaching the highest level required variety.

Some parents disliked the change because the old system was easy to understand. ‘Thirty books’ was a clear achievement. The new card had several paths and could not be summarized by one impressive number. Librarians responded by explaining that the goal was not to rank children but to help them encounter different ways of reading.

At the end of the second summer, total books recorded by the program fell sharply. If officials had compared only that number, the redesign would have looked like a failure. Yet more children attended discussion events, nonfiction borrowing increased, and families reported more shared reading. Participation remained high. The library also found that older children, who often read longer books and had been disadvantaged by a simple book count, stayed engaged longer.

The program still had limits. Stamps could not prove that a child understood or enjoyed a book. Survey responses were incomplete, and many reading experiences happened outside what the library could measure. Staff therefore stopped trying to turn the entire program into one success score. They reported several indicators separately and included examples from participants.

The experience reminded officials that a measurement can reshape the activity it measures. Counting books had been useful when the aim was simply to encourage reading, but once prizes and public success reports depended on the count, people learned to maximize it. The number became less connected to the broader purpose. The redesign produced a messier set of results, but those results were closer to what the library actually valued: curiosity, variety, conversation, and sustained engagement with reading.
translation:
市立図書館の夏休み読書企画では、一冊読むごとにスタンプを押し、十冊、二十冊、三十冊で景品を渡していました。参加者は増え、夏の終わりには前年の二倍にあたる一万二千冊以上が読まれたと発表されました。

しかし司書は、景品まであと数冊になると非常に短い本だけを選ぶ子や、大量の本を返却しても内容をほとんど話せない例に気づきました。規則違反ではありません。制度が『冊数』を成功と定義していたため、参加者がその数字を最大化しただけです。

図書館は毎回テストをするつもりはありませんでした。自由な読書を試験に変えれば楽しさを失います。また短い本自体が悪いわけでもありません。問題は、一つの数字が参加の意味すべてになっていたことでした。

翌年は、読了だけでなく、新しいジャンルに挑戦する、誰かと一緒に読む、ノンフィクション棚を利用する、お気に入りの一文を紹介するなど、複数の活動でスタンプを得られる方式にしました。単純な読了だけで得られるスタンプには上限を設け、高い段階へ進むには活動の幅が必要です。

保護者の一部は、以前の『三十冊』の方が分かりやすいと不満を持ちました。新方式は一つの数字で成果を表しにくいからです。図書館は、子どもを順位付けするためでなく、様々な読み方へ出会うことが目的だと説明しました。

二年目、記録された総冊数は大きく減りました。冊数だけなら失敗に見えます。しかし読書会参加、ノンフィクション貸出、家族での読書は増え、参加人数も維持されました。長い本を読むため冊数競争では不利だった年長児も、より長く参加しました。

もちろんスタンプで理解や楽しさを完全に証明できるわけではありません。そこで図書館は一つの総合点を作ろうとせず、複数指標と参加者の例を別々に報告するようにしました。

この経験は、測定が測る対象そのものを変えることを示しました。冊数は最初は便利な指標でしたが、景品や成功評価を強く結び付けると、人は数字を最大化します。結果は複雑になりましたが、好奇心、多様性、会話、継続という本来の目的には近づきました。
